themes.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
themes.summary: Learning across devices with fewer communication rounds and smaller messages.
paragraphs: I study local updates, communication compression, and partial client participation in federated optimization. Local updates let clients perform several optimization steps before communicating. Compression reduces the amount of data exchanged, while partial participation means that only a subset of clients contributes in each round. My work examines how these mechanisms affect convergence and the trade-off between communication and computation.

papers.note: Uses local gradient steps to accelerate communication in federated optimization.
Extends accelerated local training to support client sampling.
Studies compressed gradient differences in methods based on random reshuffling.
Studies how variance reduction can lower total training cost when local computation is expensive.

themes.title: Privacy and Robustness
themes.summary: Protecting training data and learning reliably in the presence of faulty or malicious participants.
paragraphs: I study optimization methods with differential privacy and Byzantine robustness guarantees. Differential privacy limits what the training output can reveal about an individual's data, while Byzantine robustness addresses faulty or malicious client updates. My work examines how these requirements affect algorithm design and convergence in federated learning and deep learning.

papers.note: Combines Byzantine robustness with partial client participation through gradient-difference clipping.
Provides privacy and convergence guarantees while supporting local updates and partial participation.
Studies Byzantine robustness and differential privacy together under weaker assumptions.
Examines differentially private training with orthogonalized optimizer updates.

themes.title: Optimization for Deep Learning
themes.summary: Understanding and improving optimizers for training and adapting neural networks.
paragraphs: I develop and analyze optimizers for neural networks. Adaptive methods use information from previous steps to adjust the size or direction of updates. My work includes compression to reduce optimizer memory, sparse updates that change only a subset of parameters, and low-rank updates represented by smaller matrices. I study how these choices affect convergence and the computational cost of training.

papers.note: Reduces adaptive-optimizer memory overhead through compression and error feedback.
Develops a convergence framework for randomized low-rank adaptation.
Analyzes training formulations that sparsify both models and gradients.
Studies adaptive step scaling for Muon and related normalized optimizers.
